findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is optional and is explicitly constructed as `null`/empty for bookings without a selected destination calendar. Destructuring it yields `undefined`, but the following condition reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Creating a Google Meet event without a destination calendar will therefore throw before any calendar/video event is created (and may also fail type checking under strict null checks). Guard this access, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are discarded when the primary organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: The event initializes `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. For a collective booking, other hosts' calendars are collected in `teamDestinationCalendars`, but `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` becomes a no-op when that initial value is null. Thus a collective whose organizer has no calendar configured but whose additional hosts do have calendars creates no events for those hosts, which is one of the cases this change is intended to support. Initialize this field to an empty array before appending host calendars.

findings.title: Each destination is created with the full destination list, causing non-Google providers to target the first host's calendar
findings.body: The loop invokes `createEvent` once per destination/credential, but passes the same unfiltered `event` each time. `CalendarManager.createEvent` only forwards the credential ID; it does not forward `destination.externalId`. Google happens to look up the matching credential, but the Office365, Lark, and CalDAV services all select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when creating a collective event for a second host, those services use the second host's credential against the first host's external calendar (usually failing due to permissions, or creating in the wrong calendar). Pass the current destination to the service or provide each invocation an event whose destination list contains only that destination; providers must not infer the target from index zero.

findings.title: Google updates lose the configured calendar when a legacy reference has no external calendar ID
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, the fallback now searches for a destination whose `externalId === externalCalendarId`; since that value is undefined, this always produces undefined. The previous behavior used the event's destination calendar. As a result, updating/rescheduling bookings with older references that lack `externalCalendarId` sends an undefined `calendarId` to Google instead of updating the selected destination calendar. Fall back to the destination associated with this credential (or the primary calendar) rather than searching for an undefined ID.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only selects the first calendar reference of each occurrence
findings.body: For every updated recurring booking, the code uses `.find()` to obtain a single calendar reference, despite this PR now creating one reference per host destination. It then attempts that one reference with every calendar credential, while ignoring all remaining references for the occurrence. In a collective recurring booking, events created for secondary hosts are therefore not deleted on cancellation (and the primary event receives redundant deletion attempts). Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and invoke deletion using that reference's credential/calendar ID.
